svg.title: zero-server architecture
svg.desc: A request arrives from the network at one core; there is one core, with its own event loop, per CPU core. On the core the request runs along five handler tiers, cheapest first, and stops at the first tier that answers: 0 declarative rules, 1 the core's cache, 2 a data plan the core runs itself, 3 a host-language handler, 4 a Rust handler. Only tier 3 leaves Rust: it crosses the C ABI with one call per batch to the Node, Python or .NET runtime paired with the core. The response leaves on the same connection.
